blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Courtyard by Marriott commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Upper midscale select-service: reliable rooms, functional public space, and Marriott Bonvoy distribution for corporate and leisure transient demand. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus hard limited-service boxes, Courtyard sells a fuller select-service stack; versus lifestyle select-service (Aloft/AC), it prioritizes reliability and corporate utility over design intensity.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect lifestyle lightness without systems cost; Courtyard by Marriott still carries parent systems, Marriott Bonvoy economics, and brand QA. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Courtyard by Marriott participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at Courtyard by Marriott

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Courtyard by Marriott. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Courtyard by Marriott, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; Courtyard by Marriott stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.title: P&L Implications
blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for Marriott Bonvoy participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat Courtyard stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Courtyard hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at Courtyard; amenity delivery still varies by property capability.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—Courtyard remains the brand-specific node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.title: Cobrand & Payment Scale
blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.title: Corporate & Small Meetings
blocks.body: Marriott account linkage and negotiated transient patterns support midweek compression where corporate and SMERF mix fits the Courtyard asset—confirm for this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: To Join
blocks.body: Courtyard application, royalty, program contribution, and Bonvoy assessments — confirm current Marriott franchise / development fee exhibits. Amounts are not staged without a verified disclosure.

blocks.title: To Operate
blocks.body: Steady-state royalty, program contribution, and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty assessments — confirm definitions, bases, and current percentages in the live disclosure exhibit for Courtyard by Marriott. Do not underwrite from peer rumor.

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Fee Variability
blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current Marriott franchise / development disclosure for Courtyard

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain Courtyard by Marriott's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Upper midscale select-service: reliable rooms, functional public space, and Marriott Bonvoy distribution for corporate and leisure transient demand.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

blocks.title: Corporate Corridor Select-Service
blocks.body: Suburban and corridor sites where midweek corporate demand and Bonvoy accounts underwrite Courtyard economics.

blocks.title: Airport & Gateway Utility
blocks.body: Airport-adjacent assets where reliable product and Marriott distribution matter more than lifestyle programming.

blocks.title: New-Build Prototype Efficiency
blocks.body: New-build sites optimized for Courtyard prototypes—underwrite development cost discipline against local upper-midscale competitors.

before.body: Courtyard by Marriott is a Marriott select-service brand oriented to business and bleisure demand within Marriott International. For owners, the affiliation case is business demand capture, select-service operations, renovation or conversion diligence, and Marriott Bonvoy platform participation. It should be evaluated on its own guest promise and operating implications, not as a generic parent-brand substitute or an interchangeable peer among AC Hotels by Marriott, Moxy Hotels, City Express by Marriott, Fairfield by Marriott.
